verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 56.15
verses.english: Linked Discourses 56.15

verses.pali: 2. Dhammacakkappavattanavagga
verses.english: 2. Rolling Forth the Wheel of Dhamma

verses.pali: Paṭhamadhāraṇasutta
verses.english: Remembering (1st)

verses.pali: “Dhāretha no tumhe, bhikkhave, mayā cattāri ariyasaccāni desitānī”ti?
verses.english: “Mendicants, do you remember the four noble truths that I taught?”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he said this, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha:

verses.pali: “ahaṁ kho, bhante, dhāremi bhagavatā cattāri ariyasaccāni desitānī”ti.
verses.english: “I do, sir.”

verses.pali: “Yathā kathaṁ pana tvaṁ, bhikkhu, dhāresi mayā cattāri ariyasaccāni desitānī”ti?
verses.english: “How so, mendicant?”

verses.pali: “Dukkhaṁ khvāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā paṭhamaṁ ariyasaccaṁ desitaṁ dhāremi;
verses.english: “Sir, I remember that suffering is the first noble truth you’ve taught;

verses.pali: dukkhasamudayaṁ khvāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā dutiyaṁ ariyasaccaṁ desitaṁ dhāremi;
verses.english: the origin of suffering is the second;

verses.pali: dukkhanirodhaṁ khvāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā tatiyaṁ ariyasaccaṁ desitaṁ dhāremi;
verses.english: the cessation of suffering is the third;

verses.pali: dukkhanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ khvāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā catutthaṁ ariyasaccaṁ desitaṁ dhāremi.
verses.english: and the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering is the fourth.

verses.pali: Evaṁ khvāhaṁ, bhante, dhāremi bhagavatā cattāri ariyasaccāni desitānī”ti.
verses.english: That’s how I remember the four noble truths as you’ve taught them.”

verses.pali: “Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhu.
verses.english: “Good, good, mendicant!

verses.pali: Sādhu kho tvaṁ, bhikkhu, dhāresi mayā cattāri ariyasaccāni desitānīti.
verses.english: It’s good that you remember the four noble truths as I’ve taught them.

verses.pali: Dukkhaṁ kho, bhikkhu, mayā paṭhamaṁ ariyasaccaṁ desitaṁ, tathā naṁ dhārehi;
verses.english: Suffering is the first noble truth I’ve taught, and that’s how you should remember it.

verses.pali: dukkhasamudayaṁ kho, bhikkhu, mayā dutiyaṁ ariyasaccaṁ desitaṁ, tathā naṁ dhārehi;
verses.english: The origin of suffering is the second;

verses.pali: dukkhanirodhaṁ kho, bhikkhu, mayā tatiyaṁ ariyasaccaṁ desitaṁ, tathā naṁ dhārehi;
verses.english: the cessation of suffering is the third;

verses.pali: dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā kho, bhikkhu, mayā catutthaṁ ariyasaccaṁ desitaṁ, tathā naṁ dhārehi.
verses.english: and the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering is the fourth.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhu, dhārehi mayā cattāri ariyasaccāni desitānīti.
verses.english: That’s how you should remember the four noble truths as I’ve taught them.

verses.pali: Tasmātiha, bhikkhu, ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yogo karaṇīyo …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti.
verses.english: That’s why you should practice meditation …”

verses.pali: Pañcamaṁ.
